newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Cimpor studies investment in Cape Verde.
newsitem.headline: Cimpor studies investment in Cape Verde.

text.p: Portuguese cement group Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal has completed a study into the possibility of establishing a cement plant in the West African Cape Verde archipelago, a company spokesman said.
Anacleto Fernandes Lopes told Reuters that Cimpor, Portugal's largest cement producer, would present the study to Cape Verdean authorities soon.
He said Cimpor had not yet decided whether it was interested in setting up a plant on Maio island.
Cimpor will take part in the delegation joining Prime Minister Antonio Guterres on his February 16-20 trip to Cape Verde, a former Portuguese colony.

A source in the prime minister's office said: "The prime minister wants to promote cooperation with Portuguese-speaking African countries. This trip, which includes several Portuguese businessmen, aims among other things to direct Portuguese investment to Cape Verde."
Earlier this month Cimpor bought two Brazilian cement businesses for $400 million. It also owns subsidiaries in Spain, Morocco and Mozambique.
Cimpor shares closed at 3,773 escudos, down two, in volume of 227,391 shares on Lisbon bourse.
